name: Tamara Turner
abstract_title: Consciousness Beyond the Cranium: What Sufi music and trance rituals can teach us
abstract: Considering that consciousness has a certain temporality and spatiality to it—it has a sense of unfolding across some concept of time somewhere--how might we want to imagine its expression as affecting and being affected by other temporal-spatial phenomena such as music and emotion? I ask these questions because, since 2008, I have conducted extensive anthropological fieldwork in North Africa with Sufi communities, mystical orders of Islam, with prodigious trance practices always involving music
affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Human Development, Berlin
position: Researcher (Center for the History of Emotions)
field: Ethnomusicology, psychological anthropology, Sufi trance rituals
notable: 2022 BFE Early Career Prize; PhD from King's College London; author of 'Dancing at the Thresholds' (Indiana UP)
notes: Cultural anthropologist at intersection of music, trance, and consciousness.
